plugin.name: plugin-developer
plugin.description: Builds an agent plugin from a requirements prompt, with every requirement traced to the component that covers it. Use when the user asks to build, plan or check a plugin.

prompt: Build a plugin developer agent for Claude Code. It reads a prompt that explains requirements and, based on them, builds a plugin. A plugin here is an agent supported by: commands; skills; hooks, only if the requirements need them; an MCP server, only if needed; scripts, only if needed; tests for the scripts and the MCP server, whenever either exists. The bar: a plugin built from a requirements prompt installs cleanly, every requirement maps to a component that covers it, and its tests pass. Include only the components the requirements call for, and say why each one is there. Before building, present the planned structure (directory tree, one-line purpose per component, how the agent goes from a requirements prompt to a finished, tested plugin), then stop and wait for approval. Evals: dropped for now.

requirements.text: Take a requirements prompt (pasted text or a file) and build a plugin from it
requirements.acceptance: /build-plugin with a prompt ends with plugins/<name>/ on disk and a gate result of pass, or incomplete with the unchecked steps named

requirements.text: Split the prompt into atomic requirements, each with a kind and an acceptance test; ask the user about gaps that change the plugin and record the rest as assumptions
requirements.acceptance: requirements.py check exits 0 on the file before any file under plugins/<name> is written; unresolved questions make it exit 3

requirements.text: Every requirement maps to a component that covers it, and every component maps back to a requirement with a stated reason
requirements.acceptance: req_trace.py check exits 0 on the plan and again on the built plugin, and the README table lists each component with what it covers and why

requirements.text: Include hooks, an MCP server and scripts only when a requirement needs them
requirements.acceptance: req_trace.py check reports a gap for a hook covering no event requirement, an MCP server covering no integration requirement, or a script covering no computation, integration or event requirement

requirements.text: Ship tests for the scripts and the MCP server whenever either exists, and make them pass
requirements.acceptance: req_trace.py check reports any script or MCP server that no test verifies or names; the gate's tests step exits 0
the gate's validate, build, claude-validate, load and inventory steps pass; where the claude CLI cannot run, the step is reported unavailable and the result is incomplete, never pass

requirements.text: Present the planned structure (tree, one-line purpose per component, the build flow) and stop for approval before writing plugin files
requirements.acceptance: /plan-plugin creates nothing under plugins/ and ends by asking for approval

requirements.text: A build cannot be reported finished while its checks are failing or older than the latest edit
requirements.acceptance: with a build session open, the Stop hook blocks once when gate.json is missing, failing or stale, and prints nothing otherwise

requirements.text: An independent check that the built plugin does what the original prompt asked
requirements.acceptance: the auditor is given only the original prompt and the plugin directory, and returns uncovered requirements and unjustified components, or states that it found none

requirements.text: The long build runs in its own context, so the conversation keeps only the plan and the report
requirements.acceptance: /build-plugin hands the approved plan to the plugin-developer agent and relays its report

requirements.text: Re-run the checks on an existing plugin
requirements.acceptance: /check-plugin NAME runs the gate on plugins/NAME and reports each step's status

requirements.text: Generated plugins use this repo's portable source format and conventions; scripts are standard-library Python 3.9+
requirements.acceptance: apkit validate --plugin NAME --strict exits 0 and no script imports a module outside the standard library

assumptions: Generated plugins live in this repo as plugins/<name>/ and are built for every harness by apkit.
Installation is verified live only on Claude Code; other harnesses are covered by apkit build and its recorded degradations.
No MCP server: every operation is a local command the agent already runs through Bash.

components.name: requirements-analysis
components.why: How to turn a prompt into checkable requirements and choose the components they need; holds the decision table that keeps hooks, MCP servers and scripts out unless earned.

components.name: plugin-scaffolding
components.why: How to write each component in the repo's portable format, following the conventions the existing plugins settled.

components.name: plugin-verification
components.why: What 'done' means: the gate, the fix loop, and how to report a step that could not run.

components.name: plan-plugin
components.why: Planning is a separate, user-started step so approval happens before any plugin file exists.

components.name: build-plugin
components.why: The entry point: plans if needed, waits for approval, hands the build to the agent, then runs the audit.

components.name: check-plugin
components.why: Re-runs the gate after manual edits, and on plugins the developer did not build.

components.name: plugin-developer
components.why: The build writes and re-checks many files; a fresh context keeps that noise out of the conversation.

components.name: requirements-auditor
components.why: Checks the result without having seen the build, catching a misread prompt or coverage that is only claimed.

components.name: Stop
components.why: 'Not done until the gate passes on the final files' is a rule prose cannot enforce.

components.name: skills/requirements-analysis/scripts/requirements.py
components.why: Checks the requirements file mechanically: ids, kinds, checkable acceptance, open questions.

components.name: skills/plugin-scaffolding/scripts/scaffold.py
components.why: Creates exactly the planned components, each stubbed with a marker the gate refuses.

components.name: skills/plugin-verification/scripts/req_trace.py
components.why: The two-way coverage check, and the README table rendered from requirements.json.

components.name: skills/plugin-verification/scripts/gate.py
components.why: Runs every check in order, records the result and its fingerprint, and owns the freshness rule the hook uses.

components.name: skills/plugin-verification/scripts/mcp_smoke.py
components.why: Starts a generated MCP server and proves it answers and survives its own tools.

components.name: scripts/stop_gate.py
components.why: The Stop hook's entry point; imports gate.freshness rather than restating it.

components.name: tests/test_scripts.py
components.why: Every script and the hook, against temporary repos and literal CLI output.
